ANSWER: GEMŌ MEANS “GROAN / SIGH / BEMOAN / CREAK / BEWAIL” AND GERŌ MEANS “BEAR / WAGE / WEAR / CARRY / BRING / PRODUCE / HAVE”

In the sentence, “The messenger was ordered to run for five miles on the first day,” translate, “for five miles.” ANSWER:QUINQUE MILIA PASUUM BONUS: Now translate, “Within the first year, six of the messengers had been killed.” ANSWER:PRIMŌ ANNŌ, SEX Ē NUNTIĪS NECATĪ ERANT. BONUS: Now translate, “At last, all of the messengers have been buried.” ANSWER:TANDEM, OMNĒS NUNTIĪ SEPULTĪ SUNT. 
The Latin verb form “crevī” can be understood as the third principle part of what two Latin verbs? ANSWER:CRESCŌ AND CERNŌ BONUS: Which of the following verbs does not belong by formation of the third principle part: tangō, pandō, canō, pellō? ANSWER:PANDŌ BONUS: “Lavō,” the Latin verb meaning “to wash,” is a first conjugation verb that does not follow the standard pattern of first conjugation principle parts. Its third principle part is “lavī.” Give a form of the fourth principle part besides “lavātus.” ANSWER:LAUTUS/LOTUS 
What derivative of the Latin verb “rego,” meaning “to rule,” refers to “a person appointed to administer a country because the monarch is a minor or is absent or incapacitated”? ANSWER:REGENT BONUS: What derivative of “rego” refers to “a permanent unit of an army, typically commanded by a colonel and divided into several companies, squadrons, or batteries?” ANSWER:REGIMENT BONUS: What derivative of “rego” refers to “a prescribed course of medical treatment, way of life, or diet for the promotion or restoration of health”? ANSWER:REGIMEN 
What use of the accusative case is found in the following sentence? “Multās horās in fōrō manēbimus.” ANSWER:DURATION / EXTENT OF TME BONUS: What use of the genitive is found in this sentence? “Amor pecuniae nōs ōmnēs cēpit.” ANSWER:OBJECTIVE BONUS: What use of the genitive is found in this sentence? “Ille est vir maximae virtūtis.” ANSWER:QUALITY/DESCRIPTION 
Which two states have Latin mottoes that begin with the words for “sword” and “shield?” ANSWER:MASSACHUSETS AND MARYLAND BONUS: Give the Latin motto of Massachusetts. ANSWER:ENSE PETIT PLACIDAM SUB LIBERTATE QUIETAM BONUS: Give the Latin motto of Maryland. ANSWER:SCUTO BONAE VOLUNTATIS TUAE CORONASTI NOS 
Using only two words, say in Latin, “in beautiful Rome.” ANSWER:ROMAE PULCHRAE BONUS: Say in Latin, “to great Sicily.” ANSWER:AD MAGNAM SICILIAM BONUS: Say in Latin, “I had run.” ANSWER:CUCURRERAM 
The Dark Knight Returns! Using the Latin word Batman, Batminis to mean “Batman,” say in Latin, “Batman came to this city with the strength of a god.” ANSWER:BATMAN VĒNIT AD HANC URBEM (CUM) FORTITUDINE/VIRIBUS DEĪ. BONUS: Now, using the Latin word Banus, Banī to mean the character Bane, say in Latin, “But Bane, the greatest enemy of Batman, was prepared.” ANSWER:SED BANUS, HOSTIS MAXIMUS BATMANIS, PARATUS EST/ERAT/FUIT. BONUS: Finally, using the Latin word chele, chelis, f. to mean “trigger,” and using your best Batman voice, say in Latin, “Bane, where is the trigger?” ANSWER:BANE, UBI EST CHELE?

ANSWER:POST SCRIPTUM/ AFTER THE WRITING BONUS: A pet peeve of all Latin teachers is when people misuse the abbreviations i.e. and e.g. For both of your boni (5 points each), please give the Latin and English of both i.e. and e.g. ANSWER:ID EST/ THAT IS EXEMPLI GRATIA/FOR EXAMPLE
